{{Short description| Nigerian academic}}
'''Frank Nwachukwu Ndili''' (6 October 1934 – 13 February 2024) was the 1st Nigerian [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and the 7th vice chancellor (president) of the [[University of Nigeria, Nsukka]].<ref name="Who p122">{{cite book |last1=Anon |title=Who's Who in Nigeria |date=1983 |publisher=The Biographical Center of Nigeria Ltd |pages=122 |edition=2nd }}</ref> He served as Vice Chancellor (President) of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka from 1980 until he was succeeded by professor [[Chimere Ikoku]] in 1985.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ngscholars.net/university-of-nigeria-nsukka-about-unn/|title=University of Nigeria Nsukka - About UNN ⋆ NGScholars|date=2013-07-03|work=NGScholars|access-date=2017-12-19|language=en-US}}</ref> He left the office after a long and controversial investigation by the panel of inquiry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chidoonumah.com/the-lion-goes-home-a-tribute-to-emma-ezeazu/|title=The lion goes home: A tribute to Emma Ezeazu {{!}} Chidoonumah.com|website=www.chidoonumah.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-19}}</ref> However, he is believed to have been forthright even where his predecessor [[Umaru Shehu]] (1978–1979) threaded carefully.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://campusflava.blogspot.com.ng/2012/10/university-of-nigeria-nsukka.html|title=University of Nigeria, Nsukka {{!}} School News|date=2012-10-25|website=University of Nigeria, Nsukka {{!}} School News|access-date=2017-12-19}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=January 2021}}  During Professor Ndili's Vice-Chancellorship, effort was undertaken for the first time to rebuild and refurbish the University of Nigeria following its devastation by the Nigerian Civil War.<ref name="Book of Citations p18">{{cite book |last1=University of Nigeria |title=Book of Citations on Professors Emeriti & Honorary Degree Awardees of the University of Nigeria; Conferred at its 45th Convocation Ceremony. |date=February 2016 |publisher=Senate Ceremonials Committee, University of Nigeria |pages=18}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Inya |first1=Agha E |title=Rebuilding the Den: the journey so far |url=https://nonliquidation30.rssing.com/chan-15959779/all_p4.html |website=Channel: Faculty of Physical Sciences, University of Nigeria |access-date=6 August 2013}}</ref> Ndili envisioned that the University would be destined for world-class status and designed a Master Plan to that effect. Today, the grand University entryway, the Nnamdi Azikiwe Library, the School of General Studies, and the Faculty of Arts Complex stand as testimony to his grand vision.<ref name="Book of Citations p18" />

Ndili was married to Dame Edna Odibei Ndili and they had six children - Dr. Isioma Ndili-Nwokolo, Dr. Amaechi C. Ndili, Dr. Awele N. Ndili, Dr. Ogugua Ndili Obi, Dr. Unoma Ndili Okorafor, and Dr. Obianuju Ndili.<ref name="Book of Citations p18"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=University of Nigeria |title=University of Nigeria 2023 Alumni Founder's Day Celebration & Prof. Frank Ndili's Homecoming. |date=October 2023 |publisher=UNN Alumni Association and Senate Ceremonials Committee, University of Nigeria |pages=25–28 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ndili was born on 6 October 1934 in [[Asaba, Delta|Asaba]], [[Delta State]], [[Nigeria]]. He went to St. Patrick's College in Asaba from 1950-1954. He studied at the [[University of Ibadan]] from 1957-1961 where he graduated with a B.Sc. (Hons) First Class in Physics.<ref name="Who p122"/> In 1961, he proceeded to the [[University of Cambridge]] England and graduated in 1964 with a Ph.D in Nuclear and High Energy Particle Physics. He was the first Nigerian to obtain a PhD in Nuclear and High Energy Particle Physics,<ref name="Who p122"/> having trained under [[Otto Robert Frisch#:~:text=Otto Robert Frisch FRS (1,detected the fission by-products.|Professor Otto Robert Frisch]] at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] Cambridge, UK between 1961 and 1964.<ref name="blerf_2017-03-13">{{Cite web|title=NDILI, Frank Nwachukwu|url=https://blerf.org/index.php/biography/ndili-frank-nwachukwu/|last=Udo|first=Mary|date=2017-03-13|website=Biographical Legacy and Research Foundation|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-29}}</ref> He was a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|Fellow of the British Institute of Physics]] (F.Inst.P), London, 1977 and won the Alberti Tomasini prize of the [https://en.sif.it Italian Physical Society, Erice, Italy] in 1965.

== Career ==
Ndili joined the University of Nigeria in 1971 and became Professor in 1974.<ref name="Book of Citations p18"/> His career began as a physics lecturer at the University of Ibadan from 1964-1968. He was a visiting scientist at the International Centre, [[Trieste]], [[Italy]] in 1967. He was a research fellow at Atomic Energy [[University of Warsaw]], [[Poland]] from 1967-1968, then Principal Scientific Officer, Daresbury Nuclear Physics Research [[Warrington]], England from 1968–1971. He was also a senior lecturer for physics at the University of Nigeria (UNN) between 1971 and 1973. Ndili was the Head of Department of Physics at the University of Nigeria from 1973–1976. From 1976 to 1980, he was Dean of the Faculty of Physical Sciences at UNN. In 1980, he became the [[Chancellor (education)|Vice Chancellor]]. He served out his tenure as the VC of UNN in 1985. After his tenure, he proceeded on leave of absence overseas. In 2005, he returned to UNN.<ref name="blerf_2017-03-13"/> He was conferred Professor Emeritus of the University of Nigeria in 2016 in recognition of his outstanding contribution to scholarship, and his distinguished service to the University.<ref name="Book of Citations p18"/> Ndili died on 13 February 2024 at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://leadership.ng/ndili-africas-first-professor-of-nuclear-physics-bows-out/|title=Ndili, Africa’s First Professor Of Nuclear Physics, Bows Out|date=13 February 2024|newspaper=[[Leadership (newspaper)|Leadership]]}}</ref>
